messages:
Ian (support): Hey team, customer reporting partial streaming for chat: first ~20 chars then silence. They provided X-Request-ID=req_7f3d2a and event time 2026-03-10T18:12:05Z. They can reproduce locally behind their corporate F5 proxy. Can we collect repro artifacts? :thinking:

Maria (eng): Thanks. Need the exact curl they used (sanitized token ok), SDK version, and whether there's a proxy/SSL offload in front. Also ask for OS and client environment.

Ian (support): They sent this curl (token redacted):

````
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_7f3d2a" \
  -N -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/chat/stream \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are helpful."},{"role":"user","content":"Say hello then pause."}],"max_tokens":150}'
````

They used -N and still see only the first event ("Assistant: Hello") then nothing. Customer is macOS behind F5.

Alex SRE: Checklist to gather: proxy trace (client-side tcpdump/ngrep if allowed), upstream ingress logs for req_7f3d2a, edge worker trace and response headers (X-RW-Req-ID, X-Proxy-Flush), and server-side streaming metrics for that minute.

Eli DevEx: Ask them to capture raw TLS bytes if possible (ngrep/openssl s_client) to see whether the proxy coalesces chunks: `openssl s_client -quiet -connect api.redwood.inference:443 | sed -n '1,200p'`. If they can't share pcap, ask for curl -v output and resp.raw.

Maria (eng): Repro steps for us: 1) Run local SSE curl with -N and X-Request-ID set. 2) Capture tcpdump on server side: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <customer-ip> and port 443 -w /tmp/trace.pcap`. 3) Pull ingress logs: search for req_7f3d2a and examine upstream chunk sizes and any errors.

Alex SRE: Curl variants to try (customer + our repro env):

````
# SSE (curl)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_local_test" -N -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/chat/stream \
  -d @payload.json

# On Linux, toggle low-latency TCP to force smaller packets
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_low_latency=1
````

Ian (support): Customer provided a sanitized server-side log snippet: 

````
[2026-03-10T18:12:05.123Z] req=req_7f3d2a ingress recv headers
[2026-03-10T18:12:05.254Z] req=req_7f3d2a started runtime session id=session_91
[2026-03-10T18:12:05.980Z] req=req_7f3d2a stream_flush size=128 sent=1
[2026-03-10T18:12:06.015Z] req=req_7f3d2a stream_flush size=4096 sent=0
[2026-03-10T18:12:06.200Z] req=req_7f3d2a runtime complete code=0 tokens=34
[2026-03-10T18:12:06.201Z] req=req_7f3d2a connection idle, no further writes
````

Maria (eng): The second flush shows sent=0 which implies the runtime queued a chunk but the connection was closed or the edge dropped it. SRE: can you pull edge logs around that minute and check for RST/timeout? Also ask whether any gzip or chunking headers were modified by the proxy.

Alex SRE: Pulling edge logs. Also ask customer to test WebSocket as a comparison — some proxies treat WS differently. Ian, send them a minimal Node snippet.

Ian (support): Node example I sent them:

````
// node example
const WebSocket = require('ws');
const ws = new WebSocket('wss://api.redwood.inference/v1/chat/ws?model=rw-large', {
  headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer REDACTED', 'X-Request-ID': 'req_7f3d2a_ws' }
});
ws.on('open', () => ws.send(JSON.stringify({messages:[{role:'user',content:'Say hello then pause.'}],max_tokens:150})));
ws.on('message', msg => console.log('MSG:', msg));
ws.on('close', () => console.log('CLOSED'));
````

Eli DevEx: If customer cannot share pcap, have them run `curl -v` and collect resp.raw and resp.log: `curl -v ... -o resp.raw 2>resp.log`. Offer the support-bundle command if they consent: `support-bundle collect --request-id req_7f3d2a --include-ingress --include-edge --output /tmp/rw-bundle-req7f3d2a.tar.gz`.

deploy-bot: Deployed edge-worker group A @2026-03-10T17:59:00Z (rev=2026.3.10.17:59) — rollout finished.

Alex SRE: Edge logs I pulled show connection reset from proxy 10.8.4.21 while streaming chunk 2 for req_7f3d2a — proxy sent RST after partial body. Suspect proxy idle timeout or buffer limit. Request their F5 team logs and any SSL offload/inspection settings.

Maria (eng): If proxy truncation is confirmed, temporary mitigations: lower runtime flush threshold (e.g., flush_threshold_bytes=256) to force more frequent small writes; add `Accept: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`; disable gzip on the route to avoid proxy compression buffering. I'll prepare a canary with smaller flushes.

Ian (support): I've asked the customer for: curl -v resp.raw + resp.log, node ws console output, proxy config (F5), and permission to run support-bundle. Waiting on artifacts. :hourglass:

Eli DevEx: Once we have their raw resp and our edge logs we can correlate sequence numbers and determine whether the termination is client->proxy or proxy->edge. If needed, enable a temporary extended keepalive on their connection for repro.

Ian (support): Will file a support ticket and attach artifacts when received. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
